desc: Ideation complete: Analyzed problem constraints and identified that a naive O(n^2) solution is too slow. Determined that a two-pointer approach with efficient cost calculation is needed.
Implement a two-pointer approach where `r` goes from 0 to n-1. For each `r`, expand `l` from its previous position until the cost to make `nums[l..r]` non-decreasing is <= k.
To compute the cost for `nums[l..r]`, simulate the greedy pass: maintain a floor variable, iterate from `l` to `r`, update floor and cost.
If cost > k, increment `l` and recompute cost (or continue incrementing `l` until cost <= k).
Handle edge cases where `k` is very large (all subarrays are valid) or `nums` has length 1.
Return the total count of valid subarrays.
Optimize the cost calculation using a more efficient data structure (e.g., segment tree or deque) to achieve O(n log n) or O(n) time complexity.
Test the solution with various edge cases to ensure correctness.
